recipeIngredient: 1 cup chicken broth (I use water + 1 tsp Better Than Bouillon)

recipeInstructions.text: Cut the chicken into thinner pieces horizontally, or pound them out a bit so they’re thinner.
recipeInstructions.name: Prep the Chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Season the chicken filets with Cajun seasoning. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat (I use a nonstick for this). Sauté the chicken on each side for 3-4 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 165 and the outside is golden; remove from the pan and set aside on a plate.
recipeInstructions.name: Cook the Chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Wipe off any overly browned bits from the pan. Turn the heat to medium-low so the butter and shallots don’t burn. Add butter and shallots; saute until softened and fragrant.
recipeInstructions.name: Sauté Shallots

recipeInstructions.text: Add tomato paste and Cajun seasoning; saute for 3-4 minutes until the tomato paste has developed a rich color. Add flour and mix; cook for 2-3 minutes to remove any floury taste.
recipeInstructions.name: Make The Roux

recipeInstructions.text: Add broth gradually; whisk to incorporate after each addition. Once it’s smooth, add heavy cream and whisk again to incorporate. Let it simmer for 5-10 minutes to thicken slightly. Add chicken back to the pan so it is partially submerged with sauce.
recipeInstructions.name: Finish Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Serve pieces of chicken with a spoonful of the sauce over the top. I love this SO MUCH with mashed potatoes and broccoli – see notes!
recipeInstructions.name: Serve

review.reviewBody: This was so so so good!  Added into my weekly rotation!! My kids didn’t find it spicy! Big win!
Went back for seconds even though I was already full!

THIS WAS DIVINE! Gave this to my 7 and 3 year old - not too spicy for them - and we all wanted seconds (and thirds!). Told my husband he had really missed out on this one, but will be sure to add it to the rotation. A really simple, REALLY delicious weekday meal!
This was delicious. I made my own Cajun seasoning to lower spice for the kids, but otherwise made as directed. I will definitely make this again; my husband asked for it over pasta next time!

This was absolutely divine! I ended up making this because I had most of the ingredients on hand and it knocked our socks off. The flavor of this sauce is out of this world,  not spicy (important with kids), and it felt like we went out to eat on a Wednesday. I will forever make this. Yum!!

This was so easy and so good! You can adjust the spice level with more or less Cajun seasoning (I also used McCormick brand). Keeping this one in the rotation. Going to make your apple crisp recipe this weekend. Thanks for the inspo!
This was delicious. I ended up freezing leftover sauce in my silicon molds and we used one for some grilled salmon. It was delicious on the salmon, as well. This will be in regular rotation.
This is sauce is easy to make and so delicious! Will make again for sure!
Delish! Going to make some pasta to toss with the extra sauce next time.

Okay WOW, talk about a flavor punch. This recipe had my family reeling! It was perfect in every way. 

I doubled the recipe (and decreased the seasoning by 1/4 because I wasn’t sure how spicy it would be) I also sliced the chicken before adding it back in the sauce which made serving a lot easier!

Served with roasted mini potatoes

Broiled shrimp in the oven while the sauce was building and potatoes were in the microwave. Added the shrimp into the sauce once they had some pink. One of the best sub 30-min weeknight meals I’ve  made in a long time.

This was perfect on a drizzly fall day. I served it with your instant pot mashed potatoes (minus the herb butter) and garlicky roasted green beans. I used the homemade Cajun seasoning from Gimme Some Oven (less cayenne). Did I lick the sauce spoon after putting food away? Maybe…it’s so good. I wish I had doubled the sauce!

Knew I wanted to make this as soon as I saw the recipe. I had everything except shallot and heavy cream- I used a quarter of a red onion and took a chance with whole milk (added an extra tablespoon of butter). 
It came out perfectly! So delicious with a silky sauce! Served over mashed potatoes. Everyone loved it, even the toddler and teenager. The Cajun seasoning added great flavor but did not make it a “spicy” dish. Add more if you like it spicy. 
POY has made me a better cook! Thank you!

OMG GIIIIRRRRLLL… I planned for rice-a-roni and grilled chicken and canned green beans for dinner tonight.. randomly had one cup of heavy cream left over… so I decided what the hell… this was bomb and my kids loved it (which is rare everyone loved it). As always you bought it! Ty!!!
Made it because I had it all (well, I did sub a sweet onion and half and half). I used Penzys Cajun seasoning. Yum yum yum. This would be great wirh pork or shrimp!!
